## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S1. This is audit backlog UX-01 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: /consult/:id, Prescription, Safety checks and Authorise · doctor.
Findings and reviewers: F-01 · reviewer A-02 (P0 safety; pilot blocker for prescribing, agreed by all three reviewers).
Rationale: Augmentin 625 Duo, a penicillin-class brand, was typed as free text for a patient with a recorded penicillin allergy and authorised as RX-CAEE099F with No alerts from the checks that could run. The print shows Allergies: Penicillin directly above the medicine. Indian outpatient prescribing is largely by brand and the formulary holds 23 generics and no brands, so free text is likely on day one.
Proposed UX behaviour: When a prescription line is free text and the patient has any recorded allergy, or allergies are not recorded, Safety checks raises the existing severe check-could-not-run alert for that line, naming every recorded allergy in words: Not checked against: Penicillin. Augmentin 625 Duo was typed as free text. Authorise stays blocked until the doctor gives a reason, exactly as for other severe alerts. The reason is stored with the line, written to the audit record and carried on the print. With No known allergies confirmed, today's amber Not checked note stays and no reason is asked. The honest Not checked wording already on screen stays. The rule lives on the server in the prescription safety check and the authorise guard; the screen only shows it.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, doctor view: type a brand in the medicine box; screenshot docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/screenshots/doctor-1440-free-text-ack.png. The concept's inline box is a sketch: in the product the line is added through the existing Add medicine dialog.
Components and tokens affected: SafetyChecks, AddMedicinePanel; no new component. Wording in en, hi and ar.
Front end and back end split: Back end: the rule in the prescription safety check and the authorise guard, the reason on the line, the audit event and the print. Front end: the alert wording and the existing reason step.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None in code: it does not wait for any component. Started on day one of track S.
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge: questions 1 and 2 of docs/product-ux-audit/11-pilot-doctor-validation-plan.md (brand or generic; the wording Not checked against; whether a typed reason on every such line is acceptable), recorded on the issue with a date. Safe acceptance criterion 3 of the plan applies.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low for regressions. Product risk: if the doctor prescribes mostly by brand, a reason on every line trains dismissal, so the brand list ticket matters as much as this one.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Brand names in the formulary (the next ticket). (2) Replacing the Add medicine dialog or adding an inline free-text box (forbidden until this is closed and a clinician has seen a replacement). (3) Interaction or dose checks for free text. (4) Any change to how a formulary medicine is checked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given Meera Iyer with a recorded penicillin allergy and a free-text line Augmentin 625 Duo, when the doctor presses Authorise without a reason, then the server refuses and the prescription stays a draft
- [ ] **AC2.** Given a patient with two recorded allergies, when a free-text line is added, then the severe alert reads Not checked against, names both allergies and the typed medicine, and does not rely on colour
- [ ] **AC3.** Given a patient whose allergies are not recorded, when a free-text line is added, then the same severe alert and reason step apply
- [ ] **AC4.** Given the doctor gives a reason and authorises, when the audit log and the print are read, then both carry the reason for that line
- [ ] **AC5.** Given a patient with No known allergies confirmed, when a free-text line is added, then only the amber Not checked note shows and no reason is asked
- [ ] **AC6.** Given the integration test on real PostgreSQL that authorises a free-text line for an allergic patient, when the server rule is removed, then the test fails (mutation check, shown in the pull request)
- [ ] **AC7.** Given the alert and the reason field, when they appear, then they are announced, reachable by keyboard and axe finds no violation in English or Arabic
- [ ] **AC8.** Given the refusal, when logs, telemetry and the address bar are read, then they hold no medicine name tied to a patient and no allergy text

## Test notes

- Integration (Testcontainers PostgreSQL): authorise guard for recorded allergy, allergies not recorded and no known allergies; tenant isolation unchanged.
- Playwright J2 (tests/e2e/fullstack/j2.spec.ts, step 6): Meera Iyer, free-text Augmentin 625 Duo, Authorise refused with the named alert, give a reason, authorised, reason on the print. Second case: no known allergies, no severe alert.
- ponytail-review and a mutation check, as the house requires for a safety rule.

## Notes / open questions

- Regression risk: low.
- Pilot blocker: no pilot doctor prescribes before this is merged and signed off.
